premises.text: CodeGuard backs up sites via FTP/SFTP, monitors for changes hourly or daily, and snapshots only when code changes
premises.evidence_span: we back up your site. Right now, we use FTP or SFTP

premises.text: One-button undo/revert restores prior versions for wanted or unwanted changes, including auto-repair when monitoring detects drift
premises.evidence_span: we offer the ability to undo any changes if you need to

premises.text: Git-based version control packaged as easy website protection for non-expert site owners
premises.evidence_span: Our system is built upon Git, developed by Linus Torvalds

value.text: Website protection/time machine so owners can undo damage and keep sites safe without expert ops
value.evidence_span: We consider ourselves website protection for the rest of us

causal_links.evidence_span: We only take a backup if something has changed on your site
if anything happens to your site, whether it was wanted or unwanted, that you want to revert, you can do it with just one button
we provide it for the masses

notes: Thin but complete pitch. Backup+monitor+change-only snapshots as one mechanism; one-button undo/auto-repair split as the stated key value mechanism; Git-for-masses as packaging/positioning. Beta spots/CTA excluded. Vacation/AdWords malware example is use of revert not separate premise. Three singleton-ish domains justified as separately revisable backup ingest, restore policy, and accessibility positioning.
